name: Byron Forceythe Willson
credit: Portrait of Byron Forceythe Willson, from The Magazine of Poetry · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Byron Forceythe Willson (1837–1867) was an American poet born in Little Genesee, New York, and raised in Ohio. He wrote patriotic verse during the Civil War, including “The Old Sergeant”, which appeared in The Atlantic Monthly in 1863.
He died young, in 1867. Knowles included his lyric “No More” in his anthology of American lyrics.

poems.title: No More
poems.author: Byron Forceythe Willson
poems.collection: The Golden Treasury of American Songs and Lyrics (1899)
poems.text:
This is the Burden of the Heart,
  The Burden that it always bore:
We live to love; we meet to part;
  And part to meet on earth No More:
We clasp each other to the heart,
  And part to meet on earth No More.

There is a time for tears to start,--
  For dews to fall and larks to soar:
The Time for Tears, is when we part
  To meet upon the earth No More:
The Time for Tears, is when we part
  To meet on this wide earth--No More.
